Title:
LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
38 pages, 15 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped Transformers reuse a shared block across n loops, yet inference stays costly because every generated token repeats all n passes sequentially. Cutting tied loops (n/n) hurts accuracy or collapses fixed-depth models. Exploiting a sharp serving asymmetry - parallel prefill takes under 3% of CoT wall time while sequential decode takes over 97% - we study asymmetric loop inference (m/n, m > n). Naive untying exposes a contextual representation shift between deeper prompt caches and shallow decode passes, degrading retrieval on variable-depth models and collapsing fixed-depth models or n = 1. We introduce LoopBridge, an asymmetric-loop adapter with two zero-decode-overhead modules: a learnable prompt KV bridge folded once at prefill, plus statically merged decoder LoRA when decode dynamics need adaptation. On 26.4B sparse-MoE Inkling-2 in Day-0 vLLM (29 arms, 124,816 rollouts to 1M) and 1.4B-2.6B Ouro: on variable-depth TML-d24-varloop (n >= 2), the 0.017-0.025% KV bridge alone (r = 0) lifts 4/2 by +2.8 (+9.5 MRCR 512K) at 1.75x decode speed and recovers 99.0% of 4/4 at 4/3 (1.27x), while one 0.042% zero-synthetic universal adapter hits 69.8% at 3/2; on fixed-depth models and n = 1, merged LoRA beats tied distillation by +5.7 on Inkling-2-Mini 3/2, +5.3 on TML-varloop 3/1 (p < 10^-4), and +8.7 on Ouro-2.6B 4/1 (4.2x). On 1xB300 multi-turn grids, BFCL v4 (15,200 episodes), and SWE-bench Verified, naive re-prefill loses speed and accuracy on short-output tasks, whereas prefix-cached policies sustain 1.50-1.78x speedups and preserve 2/2 accuracy without LoRA drift (+6.3 BFCL, p = 0.012), while upgrading shallow turns (Policy I semantics) beats Mini tied KD by +7.8 (BFCL) and lifts 1-loop SWE-bench from 32% (40% distilled) to 70% (p < 10^-4). Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge
